final_answer: IN A FREE MARKET, THE PRICE OF A GOOD OR SERVICE IS DETERMINED BY THE INTERSECTION OF SUPPLY AND DEMAND. SUPPLIERS ARE WILLING TO PROVIDE MORE OF A PRODUCT AS ITS PRICE INCREASES, WHILE CONSUMERS ARE WILLING TO BUY LESS AS THE PRICE RISES. THIS BALANCE BETWEEN WHAT IS SUPPLIED AND WHAT IS DEMANDED SETS THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE. WHEN A GOVERNMENT IMPOSES A PRICE CEILING, IT SETS A LEGAL MAXIMUM PRICE BELOW THE MARKET EQUILIBRIUM. THIS LEADS TO A SHORTAGE, AS SUPPLIERS ARE LESS WILLING TO PRODUCE AT THE LOWER PRICE, WHILE DEMAND REMAINS HIGH. THIS CAN RESULT IN QUEUES, BLACK MARKETS, OR REDUCED QUALITY OF THE GOOD OR SERVICE.
